q: When should we see a fertility specialist?
a: If you are under 35 and have been trying for 12 months without success, or over 35 and trying for 6 months, it is a good time to book an assessment. See a specialist sooner if you have irregular periods, known endometriosis, previous pelvic surgery or a known male-factor issue.

q: What happens at the first consultation?
a: Your doctor reviews your medical history and any previous reports, explains the tests you need and answers your questions. Most couples leave with a clear plan for the next steps.

q: Do both partners need to be tested?
a: Yes. Male factors contribute to a large share of infertility, so a semen analysis is part of the first evaluation along with tests for the female partner.
Most patients describe the hormone injections as mildly uncomfortable. Egg retrieval is done under short anaesthesia, and embryo transfer feels similar to a routine pelvic examination.

q: How long does one IVF cycle take?
a: A typical cycle takes 4–6 weeks from the start of medication to the pregnancy test. Frozen embryo transfers may follow a different timeline.

q: How many embryos will be transferred?
a: We usually recommend transferring a single good-quality embryo to reduce the risks of multiple pregnancy, in line with Indian guidelines. Your doctor will discuss what is right for you.
